disassembly_finding: hot memclr-style guest loop (stp xzr,xzr,[x17],#16; cmp; b.le) runs as ~22 emitted words per iteration: guest x16/x17 reloads from context slots 1120/1128, scratch spills, NZCV save/restore via slot 936, lsr#41+cbz window check, bias load from slot 1192, add, tagged-orr slow path, un-bias sub plus mov for post-index writeback, then scratch restores
interpretation: generation guard (0.1%) and window checks (~3%) are negligible; the dominant translated-guest tax is per-memory-op context-slot traffic from full-time virtualization of guest x16/x17 plus per-op scratch borrowing; inserted overhead is about 56% of all user-mode CPU (81.3% of the 68.9% jit-or-guest region)
next: H008: register-resident biased addressing (per-block or loop-scope scratch and bias residency) with a mechanism gate on ctx-slot sample share and paired wall screens

method: paired alternating ABBA, identical binary/bias/layout, CARRICK_DSR_COMPACT_BIASED=1 vs 0
reason: the compact lowering is 3.76% slower and loses 5 of 6 pairs; the control arm sits within 0.25% of the frozen W0, which isolates the regression to the emission rather than the aperture-disjoint bias
mechanism: compact removes the context bias load and redundant base reloads but still spills one scratch register to the DsrContext on EVERY access; the post-change census shows ctx-store64 rising 30.2 to 34.3 percent of matched JIT samples and inserted-code share rising 81.3 to 87.6 percent
disposition: aperture-disjoint bias removed from BIAS_CANDIDATES so production never activates the compact path; emission, tests and switch retained behind the explicit APERTURE_DISJOINT_ORR_BIAS constant

finding: the cost is per-access scratch spilling plus per-block-transition bookkeeping, not guest register virtualization; Go's goroutine register x28 colliding with carrick's context register costs only 0.9% and is refuted as a target
